description.value: A longitudinal fMRI study investigated therapy-related changes in neuronal activity and connectivity during reappraisal of negative pictures in women with borderline personality disorder undergoing dialectical behavior therapy, compared with healthy participants and BPD control patients.

spans.text: we investigated therapy-related changes in brain activity using a reappraisal paradigm.

value: particularly responders would show a downregulation of brain regions associated with limbic hyperarousal (i.e., amygdala and insula), a differential engagement of cognitive control regions underlying aberrant reappraisal (i.e., OFC and ACC), and an elevated limbic-prefrontal network connectivity during reappraisal of negative pictures
